1. Denial: The internet will never accept my post.
    The internet is a big, weird place. Somewhere, someplace will accept you. You just have to find it. The only way to do that is to try. It's basically anonymous anyway.

  2. Anger: Flamed/downvoated/trolled into oblivion.
    You're in a bad place, try another place.

  3. Bargaining: If I try really hard to get the perfect post, they will like me.
    You can't argue everything at once. Someone will come up with something you have not thought of, or make up BS. If you actually hit everything, you'll get "tl;dr" as a reply. Leave something for your reply.

  4. Depression: I've been posting for years and have very few internet points.
    You're still doing better than those stuck at 0 for never posting.

  5. Acceptance: The internet is a shitty place and internet points cannot be exchanged for goods and services.
    Make your post and argue/clarify later if needed, or just walk away, because who cares. Whatever you do, don't feed the trolls.

Common tips:
Do not force yourself to comment in any particular post. Find one where something good will come to you.
Find subs/posts you are knowledgeable and/or passionate about and your comments will be more likely to be appreciated.
Subs/posts on stuff you don't know much about, but are interested in are good too. Ask a question.
If you post comments on posts you find under "New" you will be less likely to find what you want to say has already been said and are more likely to be part of the conversation.

8 oz. Thinly Sliced Roast Beef

8 Slices Provolone Cheese

2 Large Green Bell Peppers

1 Medium Sweet Onion – Sliced

6 oz. Baby Bella Mushrooms – Sliced

2 Tbs. Butter

2 Tbs. Olive Oil

1 Tbs. Garlic – Minced

Salt and Pepper – to taste

DIRECTIONS

Slice peppers in half lengthwise, remove ribs and seeds.In a largesauté pan over low-medium heat, add butter, olive oil, garlic, mushrooms onions and a little salt and pepper.  Sauté until onions and mushroom are nice and caramelized.  About 30 minutes.Preheat oven to 400°Slice roast beef into thin strips and add to the onion/mushroom mixture.  Allow to cook 5-10 minutes.Line the inside of each pepper with a slice of provolone cheese.  Fill each pepper with meat mixture until they are nearly overflowing.  Top each pepper with another slice of provolone cheese.Bake for 15-20 minutes until the cheese on top is golden brown. Prep Time – 15 Minutes Cook Time – 50 Minutes
